key_evidence_profiles.finding: Hydroxychloroquine evidence in lupus nephritis is largely observational. Kidney and infection benefits are supported by low or very-low certainty evidence, which helps explain the 1C rather than higher-certainty basis of the strong recommendation.

Mycophenolate mofetil versus intravenous cyclophosphamide showed little or no difference in complete kidney remission, RR 1.17, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.42, moderate certainty; mycophenolate reduced alopecia but increased diarrhea.
Mycophenolate mofetil plus tacrolimus increased complete remission versus intravenous cyclophosphamide, RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.48 to 2.66, low certainty.

Voclosporin added to mycophenolate and rapidly tapered steroids increased complete remission, RR 1.91, 95% CI 1.47 to 2.47, about 208 more per 1000 at 12 months, high certainty. Mortality and kidney-failure estimates remained very uncertain.

CNI-included triple therapy increased complete remission versus standard care, RR 1.93, 95% CI 1.60 to 2.32, about 217 more per 1000, moderate certainty. The reviewed studies did not establish at least 3-year annual GFR loss.

Belimumab increased complete kidney response, RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09 to 2.07, about 97 more per 1000 at 24 months, moderate certainty; relapse was lower, RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.84, low certainty. Pure Class V response data were sparse.
Reduced-dose oral glucocorticoid regimens may reduce major infection, RR 0.19, 95% CI 0.03 to 1.01, low certainty, while complete remission was similar, RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.60 to 1.19, low certainty.

For maintenance, azathioprine probably increased kidney relapse versus mycophenolate mofetil, RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.20 to 2.55, and probably increased doubling of serum creatinine, RR 2.19, 95% CI 1.03 to 4.66; both were moderate-certainty outcomes.

Obinutuzumab showed a higher complete-remission estimate than placebo, RR 1.55 with sparse low-certainty data in the supplement; the guideline treats newer biologics as developing options rather than routine recommended initial therapy.

source_integrity_findings: Recommendation 10.2.3.1.1 says a calcineurin inhibitor can be used when kidney function is not severely impaired but prints the parenthetical as eGFR <=45 mL/min/1.73 m2. Figure 5 instead specifies voclosporin in patients with eGFR >45 mL/min/1.73 m2 and warns about CNI nephrotoxicity in impaired kidney function. The supplied source is internally inconsistent on this threshold.
The main guideline methods state that the evidence search was updated April 25, 2023, while Supplement Table S1 states April 23, 2023.

Several supplement plain-text summary cells contain apparent copied outcome labels. For example, Table S10's infection row refers to complete remission, and Table S11's infection and malignancy summaries refer to all-cause mortality and kidney failure. Effect rows and certainty ratings were preserved rather than silently corrected.
